mechanics.name: For the People
mechanics.currentEffect: While healthy and actively healing another Survivor without using a Med-Kit, press the Active Ability button to trade one Health State: a dying or Deep Wounded target is healed to Injured, while an injured target is healed to full health. You become injured and Broken for 80/70/60 seconds, and become the Killer's Obsession if you are not already. The perk reduces your chance of being the initial Obsession by 100%.
activation: You must be healing another Survivor.
You must not be using a Med-Kit for that healing action.
Ends/deactivates when: The active effect is consumed when used.
Ends/deactivates when: Broken lasts for 80/70/60 seconds; the healthy-state requirement also has to be met again before another use.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (5.3.0): Reduced the duration of the Broken status effect from 110/100/90 to 80/70/60 seconds.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: While healing someone, you can trade one of your Health States to heal theirs instantly, at the cost of becoming injured and Broken.
mechanics.oncePerTrialOrOtherLimits: No fixed once-per-Trial limit; each use requires meeting the healthy and active-healing conditions again. The Killer can have only one Obsession at a time.
specialInteractions: A dying or Deep Wounded target is healed to Injured; an injured target is healed to full health.
Makes you the Killer's Obsession if you are not already, while reducing your chance of being the initial Obsession by 100%.

editorial.summary: While Healthy, instantly trade one of your Health States to heal another Survivor by one state, then become Injured and Broken.
useCases: Instantly pick a downed teammate back to Injured before the Killer can secure the pickup.
Turn an Injured teammate Healthy without spending normal healing time when immediate tempo matters.
Use coordinated health-state trades to deny a snowball or save a teammate on death hook.
counters: You must be Healthy and cannot perform the activation while using a Med-Kit.
You become Injured and Broken for up to 60 seconds at Tier III.
Poor timing can simply transfer the Killer's pressure from one vulnerable Survivor to another.
pros: Instant healing can deny a down or save several seconds at a critical moment.
Extremely strong in coordinated teams that know when the health-state trade is worth it.
Can change who the Killer is able to pressure immediately.
cons: Broken prevents an immediate reset afterward.
Solo Q teammates may not capitalize on the tempo you create.
analysis: For the People ranks this position because instant health-state transfers can produce some of the sharpest Survivor tempo swings outside a direct save perk. A teammate on the ground can be returned to Injured immediately, denying the Killer a comfortable pickup if the timing is right.

The perk is especially dangerous in SWF because the team can engineer the trade. A Healthy Survivor knows exactly when to step in, the recipient knows to move immediately, and the rest of the team can cover the now-Injured user. That coordination can turn one expected hook into two mobile Survivors.

The cost prevents the perk from ranking much higher. You do not create a free health state; you move one from yourself to someone else and accept Broken afterward. In a poor position, the Killer can simply hit the new Injured target or switch to you. The perk therefore rewards situational judgment more than raw button timing.

For the People is strongest when one Survivor's continued mobility matters more than your own Healthy state, such as protecting someone on death hook or breaking a slugging sequence. It is not an every-heal perk. Used sparingly, it is excellent; used casually, it can make the team easier to pressure.
editorial.verdict: An elite emergency health-state trade, not a routine heal. For the People is powerful because it changes timing instantly, but the user must know when sacrificing their own safety is actually worth it.
